sqlite.secret_material: reject passwords, tokens, credentials, and private keys; persist references and digests only

migrations.up: create strict domain tables, append-only event journal, and fenced writer metadata in one transaction
migrations.down: drop domain tables and event journal; retain writer fencing metadata; set schema_version and user_version to 0

migrations.up: create per-domain cutover rows and append-only cutover journal; widen schema_version bound to 2
migrations.down: drop cutover tables and journal together with domain tables during rollback to schema 0

migrations.up: create append-only replay-safe control operation journal; widen schema_version bound to 3
migrations.down: drop operation journal together with domain and cutover tables during rollback to schema 0

migrations.up: bind storage dispatch intent to the action claim; widen schema_version bound to 4
migrations.down: drop storage dispatch intent tables during rollback to schema 0

migrations.up: create action leases and atomic resource admission; widen schema_version bound to 5
migrations.down: drop action lease and resource lease tables during rollback to schema 0

migrations.up: create the immutable action reconciliation boundary; widen schema_version bound to 6
migrations.down: drop the reconciliation boundary during rollback to schema 0

migrations.up: create the immutable action verification boundary; widen schema_version bound to 7
migrations.down: drop the verification boundary during rollback to schema 0

migrations.up: create control authority head, append-only checkpoint journal, and append-only cutover authorizations; widen schema_version bound to 8
migrations.down: drop cutover authorizations, authority checkpoints, and the authority head during rollback to schema 0

migrations.up: widen the control operation journal result status to PROPOSED or APPLIED, preserving every row and the frozen immutability triggers; widen schema_version bound to 9
migrations.down: no down migration: a journal row that records an applied result cannot be rewritten as a proposal

migrations.up: create an append-only signed per-domain promotion artifact journal; reject upgrade of v9 stores with unsigned promotion history
migrations.down: schema-0 rollback refuses retained promotion history; an empty promotion artifact journal may be dropped

migrations.up: record policy and target inventory digests and read-only source attestation in the same transaction as imported records and events
migrations.down: schema-0 rollback refuses retained inventory imports; an empty inventory import journal may be dropped

migrations.up: create an append-only attested inventory handback journal; the handback removes the imported records, their events and the import provenance row in one transaction so the fenced Python source can re-own the domain
migrations.down: schema-0 rollback refuses retained handback history; an empty handback journal may be dropped

migrations.up: bind the exact manifest bytes, Python source path and legacy projection directory to each new attested inventory import; first signed promotion reattests that source and projection; an older unpromoted import retains history with null binding and cannot promote until handed back and reexported; an older already promoted import refuses upgrade without inventing source proof
migrations.down: schema-0 rollback refuses retained inventory imports; older binaries cannot read v13 stores

migrations.up: bind the fenced Python scheduler target-health snapshot to the same target inventory manifest; create strict immutable health and provenance tables; reattest the scheduler source at import and first signed promotion; retain older target imports without inventing health proof
migrations.down: schema-0 rollback refuses retained target-health rows or provenance; pre-promotion handback removes health, targets and provenance in one Go transaction; older binaries cannot open v14 stores

migrations.up: add the append-only control_operator_mutations journal beside the signed control_operations journal, so an authenticated operator write is recorded with its own provenance (actor, actionId, the live cutover executionEpoch/revision/fencingToken and the writer fence) instead of borrowing the signed channel's APPLIED status
migrations.down: schema-0 rollback refuses retained operator mutations; an empty operator journal may be dropped; older binaries cannot open v15 stores

promotion_preconditions: the deployment opened the store with the cutover-authority capability (default off)
a control-authority-v1 checkpoint is installed as the live authority head
the presented checkpoint is that live tip (generation and digest)
the transition is legal, and the revision, epoch and fencing token expectations match
a canonical control-domain-promotion-v1 artifact is signed by the deployment-pinned Ed25519 key for this domain, transfer and authority tip
cutover.de_promotion: requires no authority so ownership is always recoverable

promotion_artifact.mutation: insert-only with the cutover authorization in one transaction
promotion_artifact.signer: DEEPSEEKD_PROMOTION_SIGNER_KEY is a deployment-pinned Ed25519 public key; empty refuses promotion
promotion_artifact.fields: domain, transferId, actionId, executionEpoch, fromState, toState, expectedRevision, expectedEpoch, fencingToken, authorityGeneration, authorityDigest, optional inventoryManifestDigest and inventorySourceDigest, fleetId, environment, issuedAt, expiresAt, signerKeyId, signature
promotion_artifact.history: v9 stores with unsigned cutover authorization rows cannot be silently upgraded as signed

inventory_import.mutation: insert-only in one transaction with the imported policy or target records and control_events
inventory_import.source_attestation: a live read-only Python SQLite check creates a private Go attestation token including the source boot epoch; unverified direct imports cannot promote
inventory_import.first_promotion_reattestation: v13 stores the exact manifest bytes, source path and chosen projection directory with each attested import; the first signed promotion rereads both source and projection before committing and refuses drift; a migrated unpromoted v11/v12 import has no invented binding and must be handed back and reexported before promotion; an already promoted older import blocks upgrade
inventory_import.legacy_projection: the export manifest binds the sibling .backup-policies or .backup-targets directory's exact state as legacyProjection: the file count plus a canonical digest over each file's name, size and SHA-256. The Go attester re-derives that digest from the directory (inferred from the standard .backup-control layout, or named explicitly for a nonstandard source path) and refuses the import when the directory appeared, vanished or changed. The directory is bound and rechecked, not frozen: the SQLite fence cannot reach it, so the Python service must stay stopped
inventory_import.signed_promotion: a nonempty policy or target domain requires an attested import whose transfer ID, authority tip, boot epoch, row and event counts, manifest digest and source digest match the signed artifact

linked_fence.objects: 18 triggers, three per table (insert, update, delete), named native_control_fence_<table>_no_<operation>; the global tables are frozen by any fence, a linked table only for the domain its own row names
linked_fence.python_denial: the production control connection translates the fence abort into PythonWriterMechanicallyDeniedError, so a restarted Python service cannot move the authority tip, the boot epoch or the linked intent and receipt state the transfer binds
linked_fence.verification: the Go source attester requires these exact objects byte for byte before it will read a single row, and the checked-in Python fixtures are the cross-language proof
linked_fence.lift: the linked objects survive a partial revocation and are removed only when the last fence is lifted; the append-only revocation journal remains

inventory_import.open_gaps: source read and Go commit are separate transactions; the projection directory is not mechanically frozen and a concurrent external write after the last check can still race the Go commit; existing Go shadow history and the Python control state outside the fenced set remain unproven

target_health.source: a read-only fenced copy of .backup-scheduler/scheduler.db; --scheduler-db is required for a nonstandard layout and its absolute path is durably retained
target_health.source_validation: exact Python health column types and nullability, exact immutable fence SQL, transfer ID plus authority, target-source and health digests, sorted unique rows and original SQLite value types
target_health.mutation: both snapshots and provenance are inserted in the same Go transaction; update, replace and delete guards protect the imported snapshot
target_health.public_read: GET /api/workspace/backup-targets reads target records and the health snapshot in one authoritative Go transaction; an empty response requires a real attested empty source; a v1 target import without health returns TARGET_HEALTH_NOT_TRANSFERRED
target_health.first_promotion: reread the persisted fenced scheduler source as well as the target control source and legacy projection; after promotion no retired Python source is read by the public route
target_health.handback: pre-promotion Go handback removes health and target snapshots in one transaction; Python journals scheduler revocation before control revocation and can recover an interrupted second commit or receipt publication
target_health.open_gaps: local isolated-copy integration only; native provider probes and health refresh are not implemented; three databases plus the projection directory are not one atomic store and the legacy processes must remain stopped during handoff or handback; no production, platform or exact-head acceptance

inventory_handback.mutation: insert-only, written in the same transaction that removes the imported records, their control_events and the import provenance row
inventory_handback.writer: go/cmd/control-inventory-handback writes the canonical document; the Python source verifies those exact bytes before it lifts its own fence
preconditions: the domain is still in dual evaluation and holds no promotion artifact or cutover authorization
the presented transfer ID is the one the import journal records
the imported record and event counts are unchanged, one event per row
no other writer or time is recorded on any imported row or event
no handback for the same domain and transfer exists
inventory_handback.effect: the domain returns to exactly its pre-import Go state, so a later transfer can be imported under a new transfer ID; Python re-owns the source once its own receipt is published and the last held fence releases the linked control state
inventory_handback.python_receipt: python-control-inventory-handback-receipt-v1, published by scripts/native_control_handoff.py --rollback after the source fence row and its guard triggers are removed in one transaction and the revocation is journaled append-only
inventory_handback.open_gaps: the two SQLite databases are not one atomic store; an existing Go shadow history and the Python control state outside the fenced set are still not transferable, and no production handback has been performed
inventory_handback.republication: control-inventory-handback --reexport reads the original committed immutable handback after output publication failure, without a second rollback or ownership change; v2 Python rollback may republish its receipt only from matching append-only revocation records

production_authority.source: the durable control_cutover record, read through store.IsGoAuthoritative(domain)
production_authority.self_assertion: rejected: WithAuthoritative(true) is a claim that must be backed by the durable record, and a larger epoch is never authority
production_authority.non_authoritative_path: unchanged qualification path; it does not consult the cutover record
production_authority.refusal: CUTOVER_NOT_AUTHORIZED before any durable write, with the cutover record left untouched

authority_claim.body: a control-authority-v1 checkpoint, bounded to 16 MiB and checked by the store for integrity, live chain, writer lease and deployment capability
authority_claim.success: 200 with head and advanced; an exact replay returns advanced=false without a second journal append
authority_claim.unclaimed_head: GET /internal/authority/head returns 404 CONTROL_AUTHORITY_NOT_CLAIMED before the first claim
authority_claim.refusals: 400 malformed or null checkpoint, 413 oversized checkpoint, 409 invalid chain or disabled cutover capability

mutation_apply.body: the exact canonical control-mutation-request-v2 document bytes
mutation_apply.authority: the signer public key, fleet id and environment come from DEEPSEEKD_MUTATION_SIGNER_KEY / DEEPSEEKD_FLEET_ID / DEEPSEEKD_ENVIRONMENT, never from the request
mutation_apply.refusal: 409 with the store error code (for example CUTOVER_NOT_AUTHORIZED)
mutation_apply.success: 200 with the operation result; a retry of the same operation is ALREADY_APPLIED and never applies twice

internal_api.peer: loopback-only, independent of the listener address
internal_api.anonymous_deployment: routes stay mounted but every request answers 401 INTERNAL_API_UNAUTHORIZED
internal_api.cutover_coupling: DEEPSEEKD_CONTROL_AUTHORITY is refused unless an internal API bearer is configured, so the migration authority cannot be claimed over an unauthenticated channel

checkpoints.chain: monotonic generation; previous digest must match the live tip

binds: previous and next revision, epoch and fencing token

authority.claim: store.ClaimControlAuthority advances the head; it is the only path that installs production control authority, reachable through bearer-guarded POST /internal/authority/claim
authority.deployment_gate: store.OpenOptions.AuthorizeCutover, taken from DEEPSEEKD_CONTROL_AUTHORITY, which config refuses unless an internal API bearer is configured
open_gaps: signed per-domain promotion has local Go store and HTTP tests but no production cutover or independent export/import evidence
no provider-backed kill/takeover reconciliation evidence exists yet
no production ownership cutover or exact-head release evidence exists yet

operations.result_status: PROPOSED for a v1 proposal; APPLIED for a v2 apply-mutation
operations.production_apply_scope: reachable over the authenticated internal plane at POST /internal/mutation/apply (the body is the canonical v2 document; the signer key is deployment configuration, never caller-supplied). Verification parity is complete across Python, Go and Rust (compat v32, 34 cases).
operations.production_apply_reason: the frozen control-mutation-request-v1 carries exactly one intent, shadow-compare, whose payload is a comparison expectation with no record body; it cannot authorize a production mutation, and reinterpreting it as one is forbidden. Acceptance is therefore refused once the domain is Go-authoritative, before any durable write.
operations.production_apply_contract_revision: control-mutation-request-v2 (compat v32): operation apply-mutation, payload field recordPayload, and a distinct signature domain. Applied by Control.ApplyMutation, which requires the deployment cutover capability, a durably Go-authoritative domain, the live cutover revision/epoch/fencing token, the request's actionId + executionEpoch, and the record body the signer committed to.
operations.production_apply_atomicity: the record write, the operation journal row and the control event are one transaction; a retry of the same operation is idempotent and never applies twice
operations.shadow_write_guard: shadow persistence uses PutShadow, which checks the durable cutover in the write transaction for every domain; direct Put also refuses unsigned writes to promoted non-fenced control domains. A promoted domain cannot be mutated through the shadow API instead of the signed v2 apply channel
production_apply_refusals: no cutover capability or a domain that is not durably Go-authoritative
a fenced domain (action/scheduler_run/wave/transfer) whose mutations belong to the lease and admission path
a stale cutover revision, epoch or fencing token
a record revision that is not the next one
a record body carrying secret material, or one using floats
reuse of an operation ID in a different control domain, even with an identical payload digest

operator_mutation.purpose: record an authenticated operator's write of a control record, so a browser-driven change has provenance without being confused with a deployment-signed mutation
operator_mutation.why_a_separate_table: control_operations.result_status is CHECK-constrained to ('PROPOSED','APPLIED'), where APPLIED means a verified control-mutation-request-v2. Widening it would make the two channels indistinguishable in the audit journal, so the operator channel journals separately and the signed channel stays unambiguous
operator_mutation.authorization: the authenticated operator session, plus store.OpenOptions.AuthorizeCutover and a durably go_authoritative cutover for the domain; never on the caller's assertion
operator_mutation.epoch_source: read from the live control_cutover record inside the write transaction; the caller cannot supply actionId-adjacent authority
operator_mutation.atomicity: the record write, its control event and the operator journal row are one transaction
operator_mutation.already_applied: computed-on-accept-retry; a retry of the same operation id and body returns ALREADY_APPLIED without a second write, and the same id with a different body is MUTATION_REQUEST_REPLAY_CONFLICT
refusals: no AuthorizeCutover capability on the store
a domain that is not durably go_authoritative
a fenced domain (action/scheduler_run/wave/transfer) whose mutations belong to the lease and admission path
a missing operationId, actionId or actor
record admission: invalid identifier, unknown domain, a revision that is not the next one, or secret-bearing material under the engine's shared record rule
the signed channel is not consulted or modified by this path
operator_mutation.transport_rules_not_applied: the signed channel's validateMutationRecordPayload (which refuses a float) and rejectMutationBodySecretKeys (which flags the bare fragment 'credential') are intentionally not applied to the operator channel: a stored policy always carries float placement percentages and a recoveryDrill.credentialRef, so applying either would make the domain unwritable. The engine's shared record rule still runs through prepareControlRecordWrite, and the signed channel is unchanged
operator_mutation.open_gap: no public route serves a policy create/update/delete through this channel yet, so the policy write path is not reachable end to end

policy_write_routes.create: POST /api/workspace/backup-policies — normalises the body and writes it through the operator channel
policy_write_routes.update: PATCH /api/workspace/backup-policies/{policy_id} — merges only the oracle's 18 patch fields, advances the revision the store owns, and preserves createdAt
policy_write_routes.delete_reason: this store's read path reports a record whose append-only events outlive it as CORRUPT_RECORD (orphaned control events), so removing the row would make the id unreadable rather than absent. A delete needs a terminal tombstone state that Get and the inventory list both honour; it does not exist yet
policy_write_routes.admission: the read route's Host allowlist and bearer/cookie token, then the operator channel's cutover and admission gates
policy_write_routes.state_projection: the store's state column is ACTIVE when the document is enabled and DISABLED otherwise; the policy transition table allows creation in either state and a rewrite in place, because the oracle stores disabled policies and updates them without a state change
policy_write_routes.target_bindings: read lazily from the authoritative target inventory exactly as the oracle does — only an id that is neither managed-local nor unbound needs the registry, so a policy with no registered target does not depend on the target cutover; a registry read that fails refuses the write with GO_CONTROL_TARGET_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE
policy_write_routes.create_revision_narrowing: a create must start at policyRevision 1. This store only adopts a higher baseline through the attested inventory import (allowImportedBaseline), which carries source provenance the route does not have; the oracle would store a later revision, so a create asking for one is refused by name instead of silently rewritten

companion_stores.schema: CREATE TABLE tasks (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, revision INTEGER NOT NULL, state TEXT NOT NULL, document BLOB NOT NULL)
